invoice_type.description: ACCREC is a sale to a customer.

status.description: Xero status, such as DRAFT, AUTHORISED or PAID.

entries.description: The price entries behind the cost.

known_unit_cost.description: The part of the unit cost that is known, when the cost is partial.

missing.description: Input lots that have no price, which is why a cost is partial or unknown.

source.description: Where the cost comes from, such as a purchase, a manual entry or the batch that made the lot.

unit_cost.description: Cost per unit as a decimal string, or null when it cannot be stated (see `status`). Never 0 for unknown.

open.description: True while the hold is still in force.

ex_gst_unknown.description: Invoices and credit notes with no sub-total or tax figure, left out of `total`.

not_converted.description: Invoices and credit notes in another currency, left out of `total` (never added unconverted).

total.description: Invoice revenue for the month as a Decimal string: ex GST, in the base currency, every invoice line (freight and other charges included), credit notes taken off ex GST.

is_draft.description: A draft workflow cannot be run yet.

declared.description: What was declared for the same stretch (for excise, the lodged figure), when the product has one.

explained.description: The part of the variance already resolved with a reason.

losses.description: Recorded wastage since the last stocktake.

info.description:
The Biz-E JSON API: production, stock, traceability, compliance, sales and cost.

**Signing in.** A browser session uses the `session` cookie. An AI assistant uses an access token
(`Authorization: Bearer bza_...`) with the read-only scope `bize.read`, which reaches only the GET
operations marked `x-bize.mcp`, plus this document and `/api/core/mcp/me`. Every operation lists the schemes that work for it under `security`.

**Who may call what.** `x-bize.permission` is the permission the route requires: one name, or a list
meaning "any of these". `signed_in` means any signed-in person, `public` anyone. This document shows a
caller only the operations their own permissions reach.

**Reading the `x-bize` fields.** `domain` groups operations; `feature` is set when the operation exists
only for an organisation that has that product area (`crm`, `compliant`, `costing`); `kind` is `record`, `list` or
`calculation` (a figure Biz-E computes authoritatively, which should be read, not recomputed);
`mcp` marks the operations an assistant may call; `concepts` name the business-knowledge topics that
explain the fields; `related_operations` are the operations usually read next. `schema_status` is
`documented` when the response is described and `skeleton` when only the summary and permission are.

**Costs.** A cost that is not known is `null` beside a status that says why. It is never `0`.
info.summary: Production, stock, traceability, compliance, sales and cost for a small producer.
info.title: Biz-E API

get.description: Revenue, cost, duty and margin for each product in each month, with the batches behind the cost. Revenue is product revenue: ex GST, in the base currency, from sale lines mapped to a product only; lines that map to no product (freight, other charges, unmapped items) are totalled in `unmapped`, never in a row. So this is not the same figure as monthly sales (invoice revenue, every line): don't compare the two. A foreign-currency sale's revenue is null, never converted. Revenue is sales data, so the caller needs sales.view as well as costs.view; without it the route returns 403. A cost that cannot be stated is null with its status, and the margin is then null too. - Quantity: required, must be numeric, must be > 0.
- Unit: required, must be in allowed list (see unit_conversion.CONVERSION_FACTORS).
- Optional columns: Supplier Name, Purchase Date, Batch Number, Expiry Date, Site (with
  multiple sites on: an active site's name, overriding the site chosen for the file).
- Dates: parsed as YYYY-MM-DD, DD/MM/YYYY, or MM/DD/YYYY; invalid dates left empty.
- On commit (csv_commit): same checks re-applied; duplicate batch (same org + name + batch number)
  skips that row; other rows still commit (see csv_commit).

get.summary: List wastage records for sourcemap/trace. Optional ?inventory_item_id= for single item.

post.description:
Dual-write (same transaction): updates inventory_items.quantity, inserts inventory_wastage and
inventory_movements. Consistency relies on PostgreSQL transaction atomicity—do not add external I/O,
message publishing, or async work inside this handler's transaction; future refactors must keep all
three writes here or introduce explicit reconciliation.

Transaction: SessionLocal uses autocommit=False; this handler commits once at the end (success path)
or rollbacks on validation/exception paths. inventory_items.quantity, inventory_wastage, and
inventory_movements rows for the batch are persisted in that single commit (no partial apply).

Not event-sourced: inventory_items.quantity remains authoritative (mutable cache). Movements are an
append-only audit log alongside that state, not a derived projection that replaces quantity.

Hybrid model (Option B): ledger rows use canonical item.unit; optional converted_from_unit in metadata
when the client sent quantity_unit. WASTAGE movements link source_wastage_id -> inventory_wastage.id
(unique) to prevent double ledger rows.

Drift between quantity and SUM(movements) is not enforced by the DB; see scripts/inventory_quantity_drift_check.sql
and future jobs/triggers/repository-only writes if you need hard invariants.

Optional idempotency_key with canonical payload hash prevents duplicate disposal on client retries.
Confirm/dispose UI pages are not a security boundary; validation and tenancy are enforced only here.

quantity_wasted is in InventoryItem.unit unless optional quantity_unit (or unit) is sent; then it is
converted with are_units_compatible / convert_to_inventory_unit_decimal.

On-hand quantity is stored as NUMERIC(18,4). Each line also appends an inventory_movements row
(WASTAGE, signed quantity) for replay and reconciliation; InventoryWastage remains the wastage slice.
